question.text: In the figure above, $\angle BOA$ is a straight angle, $\overrightarrow{OD}$ and $\overrightarrow{OE}$ are the bisectors of $\angle AOC$ and $\angle BOC$, respectively. If $m \angle DOC = 4x$ and $m \angle COE = 5x$, find the value of $x.$
question.explanation:
Since $\overrightarrow{OD}$ is the bisector of $\angle AOC$, we have \[m \angle AOD = m \angle DOC = 4x.\]

Since $\overrightarrow{OE}$ is the bisector of $\angle BOC$, we have \[m \angle EOB = m \angle COE = 5x.\]

Now, by the angle addition postulate, we have:

\begin{align*} m \angle AOD + m \angle DOC + m \angle EOB + m \angle COE & = 180^\circ \\[3pt] 4x + 4x + 5x +5x & = 180^\circ \\[3pt] 18x & = 180^\circ \\[3pt] x & = 10^\circ \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating an Unknown Angle Given Two Angle Bisectors

question.text: In the figure above, $\angle BOA$ is a straight angle, and $\overrightarrow{OD}$ is the bisector of $\angle COA.$ If $m \angle BOD = 107^\circ,$ find $m \angle BOC.$
question.explanation:
Since the angles $\angle DOA $ and $\angle BOD$ are supplementary, we have

\begin{align} m \angle DOA & = 180^\circ - m \angle BOD \\[3pt] & = 180^\circ - 107^\circ \\[3pt] & = 73^\circ. \end{align}

The bisector of an angle divides the angle into two congruent angles. Therefore, \[ m \angle DOA = m \angle COD = 73^\circ. \]

Finally, by the angle addition postulate, we have

\begin{align} m \angle BOC & = m \angle BOD - m \angle COD \\[3pt] & = 107^\circ - 73^\circ \\[3pt] & = 34^\circ. \end{align}

example.title: Calculating an Unknown Angle Given an Angle Bisector, an Angle Measurement, and a Straight Angle

question.text: In the figure above, $\angle BOA$ is a straight angle, and $\overrightarrow{OC}$ is the bisector of $\angle BOD.$ If $m \angle DOA = 58^\circ,$ find $m \angle COA.$
question.explanation:
Since the angles $\angle BOD $ and $\angle DOA$ are supplementary, we have

\begin{align} m \angle BOD & = 180^\circ - m \angle DOA \\[3pt] & = 180^\circ - 58^\circ \\[3pt] & = 122^\circ. \end{align}

The bisector of an angle divides the angle into two congruent angles. Therefore, we get

\begin{align} m \angle COD &= \dfrac{m \angle BOD}{2} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{122^\circ}{2} \\[5pt] &= 61^\circ. \end{align}

Finally, by the angle addition postulate, we have

\begin{align} m \angle COA & = m \angle COD + m \angle DOA \\ & = 61^\circ + 58^\circ \\ & = 119^\circ. \end{align}

example.title: Calculating an Unknown Angle Given an Angle Bisector, an Angle Measurement, and a Straight Angle
